input.question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?
input.ground_truth: Not so much a boosted immune system, but polio affected the upper and middle class far worse than the lower class because kids were exposed to the virus early on in low income areas. As a consequence they became immune to it, while the upper class kids were exposed later in life when it had a far more deleterious effect. [source](_URL_0_)

Okay! Imagine your body is like a castle, and your immune system is the group of knights who protect you from germs, which are like little invaders.

Some people think that if you eat a little bit of dirt when you’re a kid, your knight team gets stronger and learns how to fight germs better. But scientists, who are like super smart detectives, have looked and looked, and they can’t find any *real* proof that eating dirt makes your immune system stronger.

Eating dirt can actually be dangerous because dirt can have things in it that make you sick, like tiny bugs or chemicals.

So, even though playing outside and getting a little bit of dirt on your hands is okay, eating dirt is not a good idea. Your immune system gets stronger by your body learning about different germs, but it doesn’t need you to eat dirt to do that!
